entities.summary:
Gaubald (died 761-12-27) served as the inaugural bishop of Regensburg, a pivotal ecclesiastical appointment that solidified the nascent Christian infrastructure in Bavaria during the mid-8th century. His tenure, spanning from approximately 739 until his death, was instrumental in transforming the regional spiritual landscape from a mission territory into a formally organized diocese under the direct authority of the papacy, specifically through the reforms initiated by Saint Boniface and supported by the Carolingian mayors of the palace, Carloman and Pippin the Short. This period marked a critical phase in the integration of Bavaria into the broader Latin Christian sphere and the consolidation of Frankish political influence over previously autonomous Germanic duchies.

Appointed by Boniface, the "Apostle of the Germans," Gaubald became bishop following the reorganization of the Bavarian church in 739, a process sanctioned by Pope Gregory III. His primary achievement was the establishment and initial administration of the Diocese of Regensburg, one of four new Bavarian sees alongside Salzburg, Freising, and Passau. He oversaw the construction and endowment of churches, the organization of monastic communities, and the education of clergy, laying the institutional groundwork for Christian worship and governance in the region. His efforts focused on consolidating the scattered missionary activities into a coherent diocesan structure, ensuring adherence to Roman liturgical practices and canon law, thereby integrating the local church more fully into the universal Catholic Church.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gaubald was crucial in establishing the Diocese of Regensburg, one of the four foundational sees in Bavaria, which significantly transformed the region's spiritual and administrative landscape. His work under Boniface laid the groundwork for enduring ecclesiastical structures that integrated Bavaria into the broader Latin Christian world.
